main_concerns.concern: The plan treats a review request (this very prompt) as an 'implementation' authorization, which is the exact failure mode the guardrails should prevent. No actual code changes are evidenced; the claimed reality change consists of generated lifecycle artifacts and a self-serving classification, not a fixed hook.

Root-cause inversion: the fix proposes adding intent recognition logic to the hook when the lifecycle validator's existing same_session_authorized_continuation check — which should have caught this — either failed silently or was never reached. Adding a second authorization path without diagnosing the first failure creates two disjoint gatekeepers with no stated reconciliation mechanism, and risks the new path inheriting whatever pipeline defect disabled the old one.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Implement and show the real code change; prove the hook can distinguish a review-only prompt from an implementation prompt without relying on self-classification; run the regression tests before declaring the P0 resolved.

Before adding any new intent-recognition logic to the hook, trace and fix the existing pipeline: 1) Confirm the lifecycle validator's same_session_authorized_continuation check ran during the blocked write and log its verdict. 2) If it didn't run, fix the lifecycle trigger. 3) If it ran and passed but was ignored, fix the handoff between lifecycle validation and hook authorization. 4) If it ran and failed, analyze why (stale markers? wrong session ID?) and fix that. Only add new hook-level logic if the existing path is confirmed working and insufficient — and even then, the hook should delegate to the lifecycle validator's verdict rather than implementing independent recognition.
